c.tagline: Rwanda's laid-back Lake Kivu resort town, a short walk from the Congolese border and Goma.

taxi.color: white (car taxis); no fixed color for moto-taxis
taxi.fare: app-based flat/metered pricing where available; negotiated on the street
taxi.fareNote: Yego app-based cabs and motos offer set pricing where coverage exists; street-hailed moto-taxis are more common in Rubavu/Gisenyi and fares should be agreed before the ride.

emergency.note: 112 is Rwanda's general emergency line; the Rwanda National Police also runs dedicated numbers for traffic accidents (113) and fire (111). Rwanda is generally regarded as one of the safer countries in the region, but Rubavu/Gisenyi sits directly across the border from the active eastern DRC conflict, so travelers should keep an eye on the Goma border-crossing situation.

avoid.reason: On the DR Congo border (near Goma) — monitor the security situation/advisories

hood_desc: The compact commercial center around the market and main road, with shops, banks, and the town's main restaurants; the practical base for most visitors.
The public lakefront strip with sandy beach, water sports, and beachside bars/hotels; the most tourist-oriented part of town.
A quieter, hillier lakeside area east of downtown known for upscale hotels and lake-view guesthouses.
The bustling neighborhood around the Petite Barrière crossing into Goma, DRC, with cross-border markets and constant foot traffic.
A former colonial mission town a short drive from central Gisenyi, home to a historic cathedral and diocese; quiet and largely residential.
lodging: Kigufi Hill Agape Resort & Kivu Edge

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water rather than tap.

transit.hours: Local transport generally runs from around 5:30 AM to 9-10 PM; intercity coaches to Kigali run through the day with the last departures in early evening.
transit.pay: Cash (Rwandan francs); moto fares negotiated or via the Yego app in town; intercity bus tickets bought at the station or via mobile money.
transit.note: Rubavu/Gisenyi has no formal city bus network; getting around relies on moto-taxis, while intercity coach companies (Volcano Express, RITCO, Virunga Express, and others) run frequent services to Kigali (roughly 3 hours).

air: No scheduled commercial flights; nearest major airport is Kigali International Airport (KGL), about a 3-hour drive
bus: Volcano Express, RITCO, Virunga Express and other coach operators to Kigali and other Rwandan cities
ferry: Informal boat traffic on Lake Kivu; no scheduled passenger ferry service

transit.m: Intercity coach (Volcano Express/RITCO) Kigali to Rubavu

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at hotels/restaurants catering to tourists is appreciated, especially in Rwanda's more formal hospitality sector.
